chief_complaint: Management of atrial fibrillation with anticoagulation in the setting of stage 1 non‑small cell lung cancer and advanced chronic kidney disease.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is an 81‑year‑old man with a long history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and coronary artery disease. Over the past decades he progressed to chronic kidney disease stage 4 (with earlier stages 2–3 documented). In early 2003 he was diagnosed with non‑small cell lung cancer (stage 1) and began chemotherapy with cisplatin and paclitaxel despite reduced renal function. In November 2003 atrial fibrillation was identified and anticoagulation with warfarin was started, along with rate‑control agents digoxin and verapamil. He also has diabetic retinopathy, proteinuria, and anemia. Socially he reports limited contact, housing concerns, a criminal record, veteran status and part‑time employment, which may affect adherence. Recent visits (through 2003‑12‑06) have been predominantly outpatient visits focused on chronic disease management and oncology care.
